- Dynamic values: class expressions, the custom-property bridge, the runtime of under 1.1 kB
- 50 diagnostics with stable codes
- `@kirana-style/vite` for Vite 8, with hot updates
- An adapter package for every other bundler, and one for Jest; see
  [bundlers](/docs/integrations/bundlers)
- `@kirana-style/next` and `@kirana-style/postcss`: Next.js on Turbopack and on webpack; see
  [Next.js](/docs/frameworks/nextjs)
- `@kirana-style/angular`: the `[sx]` directive, builders for the Angular CLI, and a
  Vite plugin for Analog; see [Angular](/docs/frameworks/angular)
- React Router, Gatsby (`@kirana-style/gatsby`), Ember (`@kirana-style/ember`), Meteor and
  Parcel (`@kirana-style/parcel-transformer`), each with a tested example
- Server templates: the class map `kirana-style build` and `kirana-style dev` write, and
  helpers for Laravel and Symfony (PHP), Rails (Ruby), Phoenix (Elixir) and
  AdonisJS; see [server templates](/docs/frameworks/server-templates)
- The command line: setting a project up and checking it (with a bug report),
  compiling without a bundler, reports for CI with GitHub annotations, the design
  system as JSON, tracing a property, and both codemods; see
  [the CLI](/docs/tooling/cli)
- CSS helpers, each checked at build time:
  - `firstThatWorks()`: [fallback values](/docs/styling/fallbacks)
  - `positionTry()`: [anchor positioning](/docs/styling/anchor-positioning)
  - `viewTransition()`: [view transitions](/docs/styling/view-transitions)
  - `counterStyle()`: [counter styles](/docs/styling/at-rules#counter-styles)
- `@kirana-style/preset-scales`: Tailwind v4 scales as tokens, and its utility names as
  [utility strings](/docs/styling/utilities) in `sx`
- `kirana-style migrate tailwind`, proven on the Tailwind original of our shadcn/ui port: zero
  computed-style differences after the codemod and 38 hand fixes
  ([the numbers](/docs/migration/from-tailwind#measured-this-repository-s-tailwind-original))

- `kirana-style lsp`, the language server, with VS Code and Zed extensions, in
  TypeScript, Vue, Svelte and Astro files and Angular templates; see
  [editor support](/docs/tooling/editor)
- `@kirana-style/eslint-plugin` under Oxlint and ESLint, identical results, and
  `@kirana-style/biome-plugin` with the five rules Biome can run; see
  [lint](/docs/tooling/lint)
- Agent skills for writing Kirana and migrating to it, installable with
  `npx skills add`; see [agent skills](/docs/project/agent-skills)
- Every package on npm, with the native engine for eight platforms and a WASI
  build, released together from CI with provenance; the template helpers on
  Packagist, RubyGems and Hex; the VS Code extension on the Marketplace and Open
  VSX. CI installs the packed packages with npm, pnpm, Yarn (both linkers) and Bun
  on Linux, macOS, Windows and Alpine on every change

## Partial

- **`variable-default-scope`** is in the catalogue but not emitted yet.
- **Benchmarks** are advisory: hosted CI numbers, not dedicated hardware.
- **The Zed extension** works, but is not in Zed's registry yet: install it as a
  dev extension; see [editor support](/docs/tooling/editor).

## Not built

- The `slide-in-from-start` and `-end` animations, and gradients (`bg-linear-*`
  and its stops), in the scales preset
- A persistent cache on disk: deliberately not built, because the engine is
  0.05 s of a 16 s build and a cache that skips it would save nothing

## Known rough edges

- A shorthand whose value is a single custom property cannot be split, so a later
  style cannot remove one of its longhands precisely. The compiler warns
  (`unsplittable-shorthand`).
- Diagnostics point at the module that _uses_ a value, which is usually where the
  fix belongs, but sometimes the definition is elsewhere.
---
# Roadmap
Source: https://kirana.style/docs/project/roadmap
# Roadmap

Seven milestones and two decision gates. Six are done and on npm; the seventh is
1.0. Dates are deliberately absent: this is built by one person with AI
assistance, and a date would be fiction.

| Milestone | Status | What it covers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| M0: Foundations | Done | The IR, the cascade ladder, the CSS writer |
| M1: Feasibility slice | Done | Vite, React, tokens and themes, the first conformance runs |
| M2: Recipes and dynamic styles | Done | recipe(), dynamic values, hot updates, the StyleX codemod |
| M3: Developer experience | Done | The language server, the editors, lint and the CLI |
| M4: Ecosystem | Done | Every bundler and framework, published to npm |
| M5: Utility surface | Done | Utility strings, the scales preset, the Tailwind codemod |
| M6: 1.0 | Next | API freeze, a public benchmark, a security review |

Until 1.0, releases come from the work below as it lands, each listed in the
[changelog](/changelog).

## M0: Foundations

**Done.** The core every later milestone builds on:

- the workspace, the IR, longhand expansion and normalisation;
- the precedence ladder and the layer plan;
- the CSS writer and its golden fixtures;
- `kirana-style build`.

## M1: Feasibility slice

**Done.** Enough of Kirana to style a real application:

- the Vite adapter and cross-file resolution;
- `sx` for React, relations and `select`;
- keyframes, modes and themes, and the scales preset;
- the first conformance runs against the StyleX and Tailwind originals.

## M2: Recipes and dynamic styles

**Done.** Styles that depend on props and state:

- `recipe()` with slots, and finite and open dynamic values;
- the private runtime, incremental rebuilds and hot updates;
- `kirana-style migrate stylex`;
- the full component set of our shadcn/ui port built on it, which is what
  found most of the compiler's bugs.

One thing in this milestone's scope is deliberately not built: a persistent cache
on disk. The engine is 0.05 s of a 16 s build, so a cache that skips it saves
nothing you could measure, and every key it has to get right is a way to serve
stale CSS.

## M3: Developer experience

**Done, and published.** Editor and lint support, read from the compiler rather
than re-implemented, so they never disagree with the build.

- **The language server**, [`kirana-style lsp`](/docs/tooling/editor):
  diagnostics at the property, hover with the compiled CSS and the ladder step
  that won, tokens in both modes, colour swatches, a summary after every `sx`,
  completion, navigation and quick fixes. Hover answers in 1.2 ms at the 95th
  percentile on our shadcn/ui port.
- **Editors:** the extension on the VS Code Marketplace and Open VSX, and the
  same server in Vue, Svelte and Astro files; Zed through a dev extension, and
  Neovim and Helix through their own LSP configuration.
- **Lint:** [`@kirana-style/eslint-plugin`](/docs/tooling/lint) under Oxlint and
  ESLint, and [`@kirana-style/biome-plugin`](/docs/tooling/lint#biome) with the
  five rules Biome can run.
- **The command line:** setting a project up and checking it, with a redacted
  bug report; compiling without a bundler; sizing the stylesheet; the design
  system as JSON; and reports for CI with GitHub annotations. The
  [CLI page](/docs/tooling/cli) has every command.
- **CSS helpers checked at build time:**
  [`firstThatWorks()`](/docs/styling/fallbacks),
  [`positionTry()`](/docs/styling/anchor-positioning),
  [`viewTransition()`](/docs/styling/view-transitions) and
  [`counterStyle()`](/docs/styling/at-rules#counter-styles).
- **[Agent skills](/docs/project/agent-skills)**, `kirana` and `kirana-migrate`.

Still to do: publishing the Zed extension to Zed's registry.

## M4: Ecosystem

**Done, and published.** Kirana installed outside this repository, and proven so
on every change.


- **Every package on npm**, released together from CI with provenance, and the
  native engine for eight platforms plus a WASI build that writes the same bytes.
- **Installation tested on every change:** CI installs the packed tarballs with
  npm, pnpm, Yarn and Bun on Linux, macOS, Windows and Alpine, builds an example
  and checks it in a browser. Installing from the registry with Yarn and Deno,
  which CI cannot test against tarballs, was checked by hand with 0.2.0.
- **Bundlers:** Vite, Rolldown, webpack, Rspack and Rsbuild, Parcel, Bun,
  esbuild, PostCSS and Jest, each with an example, and a check that every one
  compiles the same source to the same classes as Vite.
- **Frameworks:** a guide and a tested example for each, from React, Vue, Svelte,
  Solid, Qwik, Angular and Ember to Next.js, Nuxt, SvelteKit, Astro and
  Analog.
- **Server templates:** Laravel, Symfony, Rails, Phoenix and AdonisJS, through a
  class map and a helper per template language, published to Packagist,
  RubyGems, Hex and npm.

## M5: Utility surface

**Done.** [Utility strings](/docs/styling/utilities) in `sx`, from a grammar a
preset declares as data.

- `@kirana-style/preset-scales` ships Tailwind v4's names, including composed
  utilities (rings, shadows, translations, filters) and pseudo-elements. A
  property test compiles all 7,391 utilities the grammar generates and checks
  each gives the same atoms as its object.
- `kirana-style migrate tailwind` is built on the same lowering. Run over the
  Tailwind original of our shadcn/ui port, then 38 hand fixes, conformance finds
  **zero computed-style differences** on all 189 routes of the three
  applications, at three widths, in both colour schemes, at rest and with
  overlays and menus open. The [migration guide](/docs/migration/from-tailwind)
  has the numbers and every pitfall the hand fixes resolved.

## M6: 1.0

**Next.** What 1.0 promises, and what it takes to promise it:

- an API freeze, after which a breaking change waits for 2.0;
- the full conformance suite;
- a public benchmark report under the claims policy;
- trademark clearance for the name;
- a security review of the evaluator.

Before it, one change outside these milestones: restricted overrides, where a
component declares which properties its `sx` accepts (`Sx<"color" | "margin">`),
checked by TypeScript at the call site.

## Beyond the compiler

Products built on Kirana, each released on its own. Kirana UI is there to use
with the compiler; the rest are planned, with no dates for the same reason.

| Product | Status | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Kirana UI](https://ui.kirana.style) | Available | A registry of components styled with Kirana, installed with `kirana-style ui add` |
| Kirana Docs | Planned | Markdown pages built ahead of time on TanStack Start, with a twin of each page for agents |
| Kirana Headless | Planned | The behaviour of menus, dialogs and fields, with no styles of its own |
| Kirana Email | Planned | Styles inlined and checked against what email clients support |
| Kirana PDF | Planned | Pages, margins and breaks written as typed styles |
| Kirana Native | Planned | The same `css()` handles, compiled to style objects for mobile apps |
| Kirana Desktop | Planned | Templates and checked examples for desktop shells |

## The gates

Two points where the project checked itself rather than continuing by momentum:

- **Gate 1**, after M1: does the output hold up against the originals, and is
  the authoring API worth the trouble?
- **Gate 2**, after M2: do recipes and dynamic styles carry a real application?

Both are passed. The [status page](/docs/project/status) lists what that means
concretely.
---
# Releases and upgrading
Source: https://kirana.style/docs/project/releases
# Releases and upgrading

## Today

Every package is at **0.3.4** on npm, released together. Every
release and what came with it is on the [changelog](/changelog), read from
`CHANGELOG.md` in the repository.

<!-- ::packages -->

## How versions work

**One version for everything.** The compiler, the adapters, the CLI, the language
server and the packages release together at the same number. A diagnostic touches
the engine, the lint rules, the editor and the documentation at once, so a version
where those disagree would be a version that lies.

**Before 1.0, the API can move.** A minor version may change behaviour; a patch
only fixes. Every such change gets an entry in the release notes saying what
moved and what to do.

**After 1.0**, semantic versioning: a breaking change means a major.

## What counts as breaking

- Removing or renaming an export, or changing what it returns.
- Changing which style wins: the ladder, merge semantics, layer order.
- Changing a diagnostic's meaning. (Codes and names are stable once released;
  a code may gain a better message, never a different subject.)
- Changing generated class names in a way that breaks a shared page, other than
  through the configured prefix.

What is _not_ breaking: new diagnostics, new API, better messages, smaller output.

## When you upgrade

1. Read the release note for behaviour changes.
2. `kirana-style check`: new diagnostics surface here first, and a new warning is
   usually a real problem that was invisible before.
3. Build, and diff the stylesheet. Output is deterministic, so a diff is
   meaningful: it shows exactly which declarations changed.
4. If the project has a visual baseline, compare computed styles rather than
   screenshots. [Conformance](/docs/migration/conformance) explains the method.
---
# Benchmarks
Source: https://kirana.style/docs/project/benchmarks
# Benchmarks

Every number the site quotes comes from
[kirana-lab](https://github.com/kirana-style/kirana-lab), a public repository
that builds the same three applications three ways: with the published Kirana
release, with a StyleX port and with the Tailwind original. The StyleX port is
built twice, by StyleX's Babel plugin and by its Rust compiler on SWC, so a
comparison with StyleX holds whichever one you use. It measures on every Kirana
release and once a week, so an update to StyleX or Tailwind shows up too, and the
site takes the newest run through a pull request.

The figures below are Kirana 0.3.4.

## What the numbers include

A styling compiler can be timed on a few lines in memory, or on an application.
The two answer different questions, and only the second is the one you have.
Every headline number here is the second kind:

- **Real applications, built whole.** The corpus is a demo page, sixty-odd
  shadcn/ui blocks and a page for every component, written three times, plus a
  large order table. Each number is that app's own production build, cold, from
  source. Parsing, extracting, transforming, bundling and minifying are all
  inside the time, and the sizes are the files a browser downloads.
- **The release you would install.** Kirana comes from npm at the measured
  version, never from a build of this repository, and StyleX and Tailwind from
  their own pinned releases.
- **The same pages in every build.** Before anything is timed, every element on
  every route is compared property by property, at three widths in both colour
  schemes. A run whose builds do not render alike is published as a pre-release,
  and the site does not take it.
- **A difference only where the rounds show one.** Each cell is a median over
  interleaved rounds, with a 95 % confidence interval. A ratio whose interval
  includes 1 is "level", in Kirana's favour or not.
- **What is not counted.** No input is prepared in advance, no compiler is timed
  apart from its bundler, and no figure is one fast round. The scale curve,
  generated components of growing size, is reported on its own and never as a
  headline.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Kirana | 0.3.4, from npm |
| Date | 2026-10-27 |
| Versions | @stylexjs/stylex 0.19.1, @stylexjs/unplugin 0.19.1, @stylexswc/unplugin 0.19.1, @stylexswc/rs-compiler 0.19.1, tailwindcss 4.3.3, @tailwindcss/vite 4.3.3, vite 8.3.4, react 19.3.1 |
| Machine | GitHub-hosted runner, 4 cores (AMD EPYC 7763), 16 GB, Linux 7.0.0-1017-azure |
| Tools | Node.js 26.3.0, Bun 1.4.3, Chrome 156.0.8078.47 |
| Rounds | 10 cold builds per app after 1 warm-up; 20 browser runs; 20 rounds at each large-dom size; 10 cold builds at each scale-curve size |
| Scale curve | its own GitHub-hosted runner, 4 cores (AMD EPYC 7763), 16 GB |
| Conformance | web passed, blocks passed, examples passed, large-dom passed, scale-curve/100 passed, scale-curve/1000 passed, scale-curve/10000 passed |
| Run | https://github.com/kirana-style/kirana-lab/actions/runs/40436762408 |

## How to read it

Each cell is the median of every round. **Kirana ÷ StyleX** is Kirana's median
over StyleX's, so below 1 is lower for Kirana, and lower is better for every
measure. Beside each ratio is its 95 % confidence interval, from resampling the
rounds, and a difference is called one only when that interval excludes 1. A
ratio whose interval includes 1 is "no clear difference", and the site words it
as "level".

**StyleX** is the port built by StyleX's Babel plugin, and **StyleX (SWC)** the
same port built by `@stylexswc/unplugin`. Where the site makes one claim about
StyleX, it compares Kirana with whichever of the two Kirana does less well
against on that measure, and names it.

Before anything is timed, the builds of each app are crawled and compared
property by property, at three widths in both colour schemes; the SWC build is
compared with the Babel one. A run whose builds
do not render alike publishes its numbers as a pre-release, and the site does not
take them.

## Where Kirana is behind

Every measure on which Kirana measured higher, by its interval:

- CSS, apps/web: 1.09× StyleX (1.09–1.09)
- CSS, apps/web: 1.07× StyleX (SWC) (1.07–1.07)
- CSS, apps/blocks: 1.06× StyleX (1.06–1.06)
- CSS, apps/blocks: 1.04× StyleX (SWC) (1.04–1.04)
- CSS, apps/examples: 1.09× StyleX (1.09–1.09)
- CSS, apps/examples: 1.07× StyleX (SWC) (1.07–1.07)
- CSS, all three apps: 1.08× StyleX (1.08–1.08)
- CSS, all three apps: 1.06× StyleX (SWC) (1.06–1.06)
- JavaScript, apps/blocks: 1.002× StyleX (SWC) (1.002–1.002)
- JavaScript, gzip, apps/examples: 1.004× Tailwind (1.004–1.004)
- Layout, apps/web, CPU throttled 6×, about 6211 elements: 1.13× StyleX (1.01–1.22)
- JavaScript, apps/large-dom: 1.000× StyleX (SWC) (1.000–1.000)
- HTML, the large-dom table, 1,000 rows: 1.11× StyleX (1.11–1.11)
- HTML, the large-dom table, 1,000 rows: 1.11× StyleX (SWC) (1.11–1.11)
- class attributes, the large-dom table, 1,000 rows: 1.27× StyleX (1.27–1.27)
- class attributes, the large-dom table, 1,000 rows: 1.27× StyleX (SWC) (1.27–1.27)
- JavaScript heap, the large-dom table, 1,000 rows, CPU throttled 4×, about 22552 elements: 1.006× Tailwind (1.003–1.009)

- HTML, the large-dom table, 5,000 rows: 1.11× StyleX (SWC) (1.11–1.11)
- class attributes, the large-dom table, 5,000 rows: 1.27× StyleX (1.27–1.27)
- class attributes, the large-dom table, 5,000 rows: 1.27× StyleX (SWC) (1.27–1.27)
- Filter, to the next frame, the large-dom table, 5,000 rows, CPU throttled 4×, about 112608 elements: 1.07× Tailwind (1.03–1.11)
- Filter, layout, the large-dom table, 5,000 rows, CPU throttled 4×, about 112608 elements: 1.52× Tailwind (1.25–1.62)
- Every row again, style recalc, the large-dom table, 5,000 rows, CPU throttled 4×, about 112608 elements: 1.05× StyleX (SWC) (1.03–1.08)
- JavaScript heap, the large-dom table, 5,000 rows, CPU throttled 4×, about 112608 elements: 1.03× Tailwind (1.03–1.03)
- Build, cold, the scale curve, 1,000 components: 1.18× Tailwind (1.15–1.20)
- Build, cold, the scale curve, 10,000 components: 1.75× Tailwind (1.71–1.81)

## Build and output

Builds are each app's own `vite build`, cold (its output and Vite's cache removed
first), and interleaved, so a round builds Kirana, StyleX, StyleX (SWC) and
Tailwind in turn and a machine that slows down slows them all. Sizes are every client asset of the
type, each compressed on its own as a browser receives it: gzip at level 9,
brotli at quality 11.

## In the browser

The `web` app is grown to the same number of elements in each build, the CPU is
throttled, and Chrome's own counters are read through the DevTools protocol: the
style recalculation when the colour scheme switches, a hover, layout, and the
95th percentile of frame times.

### CPU throttled 4×

## A large page

The demos above are small pages. The large-dom corpus is an order table of
thousands of rows, as an admin screen has, written in each implementation with its
own components: a status badge, a select, an icon button, and an Approve button on
pending orders. Every build renders the same rows, from one seeded generator.

Each round filters the table to the overdue orders and back to all of them, each
timed from the click to the next frame, scrolls through it, moves the pointer
across rows, and reads the JavaScript heap after a garbage collection. The page's
HTML and `class` attributes are its size.

**The app's build**

| Measure | Kirana | StyleX | StyleX (SWC) | Tailwind | Kirana ÷ StyleX | Kirana ÷ StyleX (SWC) | Kirana ÷ Tailwind |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

| CSS, gzip | 8.1 kB | 9.3 kB | 9.4 kB | 26.8 kB | 0.87× (0.87–0.87) lower | 0.87× (0.87–0.87) lower | 0.30× (0.30–0.30) lower |

## The same components, more of them

The scale curve asks how the cost grows. A generator writes the same components
for every implementation, each in its own idiom: tokens, a recipe and a font size
with its line height in every one, and in fixed shares a hover state, a
breakpoint, a relation and a value known only at runtime. Each size is built cold,
and the curve is read across the sizes, never from one of them. It runs on a
runner of its own beside the rest, so compare its numbers with each other, not
with the tables above.

**Build, cold, at every size**

|  | 100 | 1,000 | 10,000 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Kirana | 2.44 s | 4.00 s | 20.26 s |
| StyleX | 9.85 s | 60.39 s | 607.47 s |
| StyleX (SWC) | 3.89 s | 8.66 s | 58.25 s |
| Tailwind | 2.63 s | 3.40 s | 11.60 s |
| Kirana ÷ StyleX | 0.25× (0.24–0.25) lower | 0.07× (0.07–0.07) lower | 0.03× (0.03–0.03) lower |
| Kirana ÷ StyleX (SWC) | 0.63× (0.62–0.63) lower | 0.46× (0.45–0.47) lower | 0.35× (0.34–0.35) lower |
| Kirana ÷ Tailwind | 0.93× (0.91–0.93) lower | 1.18× (1.15–1.20) higher | 1.75× (1.71–1.81) higher |

## What it does not say

- **The machine is a shared CI runner.** Absolute times move from run to run,
  and GitHub does not promise the same processor twice: the run above names the
  one it had. Compare ratios within one run, never times from two runs.
- **The applications are one shadcn/ui port.** Many small components, shared
  tokens, and one large table. A codebase with other habits may measure
  otherwise, and the lab's corpus will grow.
- **The editor is not measured here yet.** The language server's latency and the
  time from saving a file to the updated stylesheet are from one developer
  machine, in
  [the benchmark notes](https://github.com/kirana-style/kirana/blob/main/packages/kirana/design-notes/benchmark-results.md).

The rules a quoted number has to meet, the fairness checks and the statistics are
in the lab's
[METHODOLOGY.md](https://github.com/kirana-style/kirana-lab/blob/main/METHODOLOGY.md).

Each one has an example CI builds and checks in a browser on every change.

| Bundler                        | Package                                                         |
| ------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------- |

| webpack 5                      | `@kirana-style/webpack`, with dev-server updates                |
| Rspack, Rsbuild                | `@kirana-style/rspack`, with dev-server updates                 |

## Frameworks

Every framework has a guide and a tested example; the
[frameworks page](/docs/frameworks/overview) picks yours.

| Framework                                  | How styles reach the markup                                     |
| ------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| React 19, TanStack Start                   | `sx` compiles to `className`; this site is a TanStack Start app |
| Preact, Solid, Qwik 2                      | `sx` compiles to `class`                                        |
| Vue, Nuxt, Svelte, SvelteKit, Astro        | `sx` in their templates                                         |
| Angular (CLI and Analog)                   | `[sx]` in templates, merged at runtime                          |
| React Router, Gatsby, Ember, Meteor        | as their component layer does                                   |
| No framework                               | handles are class strings                                       |
| Laravel, Symfony, Rails, Phoenix, AdonisJS | templates read a [class map](/docs/frameworks/server-templates) |

## Runtime and distribution

| What runs it                                     | Detail                                                                                                  |
| ------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Node.js ≥ 22.18, Bun, Deno                       | Any of them runs the compiler and the command line                                                      |
| Native engine (Node-API)                         | A prebuilt package per platform on npm, eight in all, install-tested in CI                              |
| WASI fallback (WebContainers, no native addon)   | `@kirana-style/compiler-wasm32-wasi`, with byte-identical output                                        |
| A browser page (playgrounds, editors on the web) | `@kirana-style/compiler-browser`: the WASI engine with an in-memory project, byte-identical in Chromium |

## Configuration keys in the specification but not the build

- `presets`, to compose preset packages. Import preset modules directly instead.

It fails validation today. (`libraries` works: see
[publishing a library](/docs/building/libraries).) See the [roadmap](/docs/project/roadmap) for when they
are scheduled.

# Contributing
Source: https://kirana.style/docs/project/contributing
# Contributing to Kirana

Thank you for wanting to help. Kirana is small and independent, so every good
bug report, docs fix and pull request moves it noticeably. This page says what
helps most and how to get a change merged without a round of back-and-forth.

The same guide is `CONTRIBUTING.md` in the repository, and the ways to support
the project with money are on the [sponsors page](/sponsors).

## Report a bug

The most valuable contribution at this stage. A good report has:

- **What you ran**: the Kirana version, your framework and bundler, and the
  smallest source that shows the problem.
- **What you expected and what happened**: the computed style you expected,
  and the one you got. `kirana-style trace <file>:<line> <property>` prints every
  entry for a style and the one that won; paste its output.
- **The diagnostic**, if there was one, with its code (`KRN…`).

A style that compiles and renders wrong is a bug even when no diagnostic fired;
report it. So is a diagnostic whose help text did not tell you what to do.

## Improve the docs

If a page made you guess, it is wrong. Open an issue naming the page and the
sentence, or send the fix. Docs live in `apps/docs/content/docs/`; run
`bun run generate` in `apps/docs` after editing, so the generated pages and the
search index follow.

Every statement in the docs should be true of the code today. A claim about
performance, size or another project needs a source or a measurement beside it.

## Change the code

### Before you start

**Open an issue first** for anything beyond a small, obvious fix, and wait for a
maintainer to agree on the approach. It saves you writing a pull request that
cannot be merged. Pull requests that only reformat, rename or reorder code are
not accepted: the formatters and linters own that.

### Set up

```bash
vp install             # dependencies, and the git hooks
vp run check           # format, lint, types, docs consistency
vp run rust            # cargo fmt, Clippy, cargo-deny, Rust tests
vp run test            # Vitest
vp run build           # native engine, then the docs site
```

Vite+ (`vp`) and Rust (through rustup) are the two installs. The README's
Scripts table lists what each command needs. The pre-push hook (`vp run prepush`)
runs the checks, the Rust lints, the tests with 100 % coverage, the Zed
extension's own Rust checks and the budgets, from the cache when nothing changed.

### Try it on this repository

Every component in `packages/ui` is written with Kirana. Open one, say
`packages/ui/src/components/badge.tsx`: style handles at the top, an `sx` prop on the elements
below. Then start this site and change a value in any `css({ … })` call:

```console
$ bun dev
```

The page on <http://localhost:3000> updates without a reload: the compiler rebuilds the stylesheet
and sends it through Vite's hot update channel. To ask the compiler what it found, and which
declaration wins a property and why:

```console
$ node packages/kirana/npm/cli/bin/kirana-style.ts check packages/ui/src
$ node packages/kirana/npm/cli/bin/kirana-style.ts trace packages/ui/src/components/badge.tsx:12 color
```

`trace` prints one line per candidate declaration, marks the winner, and names the step of the
[precedence ladder](/docs/styling/precedence) that decided it.

### What a pull request needs

- **Tests, and 100 % coverage.** Kirana's packages keep 100 % coverage of Rust
  lines, functions and regions, and of TypeScript statements, branches, functions
  and lines. `vp run coverage` checks it. A change that lowers it fails CI.
- **The budgets record, when the output or the types change.** It records:
  - what the compiler's output weighs: each golden fixture, `packages/ui`,
    `packages/docs-ui` and the runtime, raw, gzip and brotli;
  - how many types and instantiations checking the API costs.

  A change to either fails `vp run budgets` until `bun run budgets --update` in
  `packages/kirana` rewrites the record. Commit it with the change, so the diff
  shows what moved; CI prints the difference as a table in the job summary.

- **The specification, in the same change.** A change to the compiler's
  behaviour updates the matching document in `spec/`, and a design choice gets
  a decision in `spec/20-decisions.md`.
- **The docs, in the same change.** A new token, diagnostic, option or
  behaviour is not finished until `apps/docs` says so.
- **Evidence for a trade-off.** If your change makes something worse to make
  something else better, show the failing case, the numbers and a test.
- **A sign-off on every commit.** Contributions are accepted under the
  [Developer Certificate of Origin](https://developercertificate.org/): add
  `Signed-off-by: Your Name <you@example.com>` with `git commit -s`, certifying
  you have the right to submit the work under the project's licence.

### Security

- Do not change files under `.github/workflows/` in the same pull request as
  other work; a workflow change is reviewed on its own.
- Report a vulnerability privately, never in a public issue: see `SECURITY.md`.
- CI actions and runner images are pinned to an exact version, never written
  from memory: check the action's latest release and that it runs on a
  supported runtime.

## Support the project

Kirana is MIT licensed and free to use. If it saves you time,
[the sponsors page](/sponsors) lists every way to support it (GitHub Sponsors,
Open Collective, Polar, and invoices for companies) once each channel opens.

## Conduct

Be kind, be specific, and assume good intent. Critique code and ideas, never
people. The full code of conduct is the Contributor Covenant, in
`CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md`.

# For LLMs
Source: https://kirana.style/docs/project/llms
# For LLMs

Every page of this site is also served as markdown, and the whole set is served
as two plain-text files. They come from the same parse as the pages you are
reading, in the same build, so they cannot drift.

Kirana is new enough that a model's training data does not contain it. Pointing
a coding agent at these files is the difference between it writing Kirana and it
writing something that looks like Tailwind.

## The endpoints

| URL               | What it is                                                                            |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `/llms.txt`       | The index: one line per page, with its description and a link to that page's markdown |
| `/llms-full.txt`  | Every page, in reading order, as one file                                             |
| `/docs/<path>.md` | One page as markdown, such as `/docs/styling/merging.md`                              |

`/docs/index.md` is the introduction. The markdown twin of a page carries its
title and canonical URL in a two-line header, then the page body exactly as it
was written.

## Which one to use

**`/llms.txt` first.** It is small, and it lets an agent choose the pages it
actually needs rather than spending its context on all of them.

**A single page** when you know the topic. Merging, precedence, conditions and
the API reference answer most questions on their own.

**`/llms-full.txt`** when you want the whole documentation in one context
window, or when you are building an index of your own.

> [!TIP] Start with these four
> `/docs/start/mental-model.md`, `/docs/styling/styles.md`,
> `/docs/styling/merging.md` and `/docs/reference/api.md` cover the parts an
> agent gets wrong without them: that styles are typed objects, that conditions
> live inside the value, and that a later style replaces entries rather than
> whole properties.

## Giving an agent the rules

The documentation explains Kirana; it does not, by itself, stop an agent
reaching for habits from other systems. The [agent skills](/docs/project/agent-skills)
do that part: install them, and the agent loads the rules, the
check-trace-report loop and the diagnostics reference by itself. The four rules worth stating outright in
your own prompt or project instructions:

- Styles are `css({ ... })` handles. There is no `cn`, no
  `class-variance-authority`, and no utility-class strings.
- Conditions go **inside the value**: `color: { base: a, ":hover": b }`, not a
  `:hover` key at the top level.
- Dark mode is a `light-dark()` pair on the token. There is no `dark:` variant
  and no second stylesheet.
- A later style **replaces the entries it names** and keeps the rest. To drop a
  property's other entries, write `{ "*": null, base: ... }`.

Everything the compiler can catch, it catches: a mistake in any of these is a
diagnostic with a code, not a silently wrong style. The
[diagnostics reference](/docs/tooling/diagnostics) lists all of them, and it is
worth handing to an agent alongside the pages above.

## Machine-readable extras

- The diagnostics are also available as data on the
  [diagnostics page](/docs/tooling/diagnostics): code, message, and what to do
  about it.
- [`kirana-style export`](/docs/tooling/cli#kirana-style-export) prints your project's own
  design system (tokens, themes, recipes and relations, with where each is
  declared) as JSON, so an agent uses the names that exist.
- The [API reference](/docs/reference/api) is generated from the packages'
  type declarations, so its signatures are the real ones.
- The [playground](/play) shows curated examples with the CSS, class names and
  diagnostics the real compiler produced from them at build time. It does not
  compile pasted source yet (that needs the WASM engine), so to check an agent's
  suggestion, run `kirana-style build` or `kirana-style check` on it.
---
# Agent skills
Source: https://kirana.style/docs/project/agent-skills
# Agent skills

A model's training data does not contain Kirana, so a coding agent left to itself
writes Tailwind or StyleX and calls it Kirana. The [plain-text docs](/docs/project/llms)
explain the system; the two skills in Kirana's repository tell an agent how to
work in it: what to check first, which mistakes compile and still render wrong,
and what to run when something does.

```bash
npx skills add kirana-style/kirana                 # both
npx skills add kirana-style/kirana --skill kirana  # one
```

The [`skills`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills) command installs them for
the agent you use (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, OpenCode and the others it
supports), in your project or globally with `-g`, and `npx skills update` keeps
them current.

They live in the repository's `skills/` folder; until the repository is public,
point the command at a checkout instead (`npx skills add ./kirana`).

## What each one teaches

| Skill            | When the agent loads it                                                         | What it carries                                                                                          |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `kirana`         | the project imports `@kirana-style/core`, or a style compiles and renders wrong | the rules that cause real bugs, the loop below, where each new thing goes, and the habits to unlearn     |
| `kirana-migrate` | asked to port components or an app from Tailwind, shadcn/ui or StyleX           | the codemods and their reports, the traps in both directions, and how to prove the port renders the same |

Each skill is short (the rules and the workflow), and keeps the detail in
reference files the agent reads only when it needs them: the API, how `sx` is
spelled in each framework, the Tailwind and StyleX mappings, and two files
generated from the compiler's source on every build: every
[diagnostic](/docs/tooling/diagnostics) with what to do about it, and every
[lint rule](/docs/tooling/lint) with the linters that run it. A diagnostic added
to the compiler without a line saying what to do about it fails the build.

## The loop it follows

1. **Learn the project.** Run [`kirana-style export`](/docs/tooling/cli#kirana-style-export)
   for the tokens, themes, recipes and relations that exist, by their real names,
   then `kirana-style doctor`.
2. **Write the style**, with the rules: conditions inside the value, entries
   merge per condition, `sx` forwarded last, `styleProps` for installed
   components, colours as `light-dark()` pairs.
3. **`kirana-style check`**, and fix every error by its code.
4. **Lint**, with whichever of ESLint, Oxlint or Biome the project runs.
5. **`kirana-style trace file:line property`** when it compiles and looks wrong.
6. **`kirana-style doctor --report`** when it looks like a Kirana bug, and ask before
   filing it.

Every step answers from the compiler, so an agent that follows it checks its own
work instead of guessing whether a class string it remembered still exists.

## With llms.txt

The skills and the [plain-text docs](/docs/project/llms) do different jobs. A
skill is instructions an agent loads by itself when the task matches; `llms.txt`
is reference it reads when it needs to know more. The skills link to the
markdown pages instead of copying them, so the two never disagree.
